source.title: Boss Up: Boss Battle Design Fundamentals and Retrospective
source.speaker: Itay Keren

translation.title: Boss Up: 10 checks for an encounter
translation.intro: A practical adaptation of Itay Keren’s talk. Use these cards as a review pass: each one points to an atlas lens that makes the idea reusable.
translation.lensSectionIntro: This lens connects to one of the talk’s practical rules.

translation.title: Reward the journey
translation.body: Make the confrontation feel like a fresh reward, not time added between the player and progress.

translation.title: Frame the story
translation.body: Build anticipation before the challenge and give its success or failure a meaningful aftermath.

translation.title: Fit context and sequence
translation.body: Connect place, supporting actors, timing, neighboring challenges, and consequences into one setup.

translation.title: Test and teach deliberately
translation.body: Check recently learned skills; introduce a new one only with focused attention and a reason to use it.

translation.title: Design the survivable space
translation.body: Start with where and how the player can remain alive, then build threats around that response space.

translation.title: Make state legible
translation.body: Show the goal, valid hits, progress, signals, and enough reaction time; mystery can be intentional, helplessness should not be.

translation.title: Preserve expression
translation.body: Let different tools, skills, and player archetypes produce viable approaches where the system supports them.

translation.title: Change phase with purpose
translation.body: Transition for a mechanical change, skill combination, story beat, or mental break—not just more duration.

translation.title: Shape difficulty as rhythm
translation.body: Use peaks, relief, visible progress, and a foreseeable ending to turn expected failure into expected triumph.

translation.title: Break rules with intent
translation.body: Exceptional rules, viewpoints, or mechanics can dazzle, but they must serve reward, engagement, or challenge.
